name: Gibeon
overview: Gibeon was a significant Hivite city that strategically secured a treaty with Joshua by deceiving the Israelites, as recorded when its inhabitants heard of Israel's victories over Jericho and Ai. Though their cunning was uncovered, Joshua assigned them to serve the congregation by drawing water and cutting wood for the altar of the LORD. Gibeon was allotted to the tribe of Benjamin and served as a central location during Israel's conquest, notably where Joshua commanded the sun to stand still in the LORD's deliverance of the Amorites. The city’s importance continued as a religious center with the tabernacle and as a site of worship and sacrifice.
